scene:
Three zones read left to right, separated by generous space.

LEFT ZONE, changing owners behind one manager: at the top a wide navy signboard over a doorway labelled SAME MANAGER. Below it a horizontal timeline arrow pointing right with three dots labelled 2006, 2017 and 2023. Under the timeline, small investor figures carrying briefcases walk away downward-left along an ochre arrow pointing away from the timeline, labelled INVESTORS LEAVE; other small investor figures walk in from the lower right along a teal arrow pointing toward the timeline, labelled INVESTORS JOIN. The point: the sign stays, the people behind it change.

MIDDLE ZONE, a group that keeps buying: a large central hub building drawn with server racks and a padlock shield, labelled SHARED SUPPORT. Around it, six small separate office buildings each with its own tiny steering wheel, connected to the hub by thin lines; one caption under the ring of small buildings labelled LOCAL DECISIONS. Above the hub, a row of small purchase tags with a shopping-cart icon labelled 33 ACQUISITIONS IN 2024.

RIGHT ZONE, one year, two profit figures: a simple bridge chart of three navy-outlined bars. First a tall teal bar labelled EBITDA €893M. Then a thin ochre bar floating on top of its level, labelled M&A COSTS +€11.665M. Then a slightly taller teal bar labelled ADJUSTED €904M. Next to the ochre bar, an empty open wallet with a small navy cross, labelled NO NEW CASH. Below the chart, a calendar page for the next year with a question mark and a small cart icon, labelled WHO FUNDS NEXT YEAR?

TEXT: draw exactly these labels, each once and nothing else: SAME MANAGER, 2006, 2017, 2023, INVESTORS LEAVE, INVESTORS JOIN, SHARED SUPPORT, LOCAL DECISIONS, 33 ACQUISITIONS IN 2024, EBITDA €893M, M&A COSTS +€11.665M, ADJUSTED €904M, NO NEW CASH, WHO FUNDS NEXT YEAR?. Any other text is a defect.
alt: A signboard labelled same manager stays fixed over a 2006, 2017 and 2023 timeline while investors leave and others join; a shared-support hub serves small local businesses after 33 acquisitions in 2024; a bridge chart goes from €893 million of EBITDA plus €11.665 million of M&A costs to €904 million adjusted, with an empty wallet marking no new cash and a question about who funds next year's deals.
caption: Behind a familiar manager the investors changed; a group that keeps buying companies reports one year's profit two ways, and neither answers who funds the next deals.
